NADIA BRENNAN-AZIZ
Senior Platform / Site Reliability Engineer
Manchester, UK | nadia.brennanaziz@example.com | +44 7700 900909 | github.com/nba-sre-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior platform and site reliability engineer with 10 years of infrastructure experience, including six years operating Kubernetes platforms on AWS. Hands-on experience designing, building and operating cloud infrastructure with Terraform, and leading platform initiatives from technical proposal through production. Builds reliable, observable platforms and self-service tools that help product teams deploy and operate services effectively. Experienced in technical leadership, incident management, SLOs and cross-functional work with product leadership.

CORE SKILLS
Cloud infrastructure: AWS (EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront), cloud environment design and operation
Infrastructure as code: Terraform, Atlantis, Crossplane
Platforms and orchestration: Kubernetes, Helm, Kustomize, Argo CD, Karpenter
Reliability and observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Alertmanager, OpenTelemetry, SLOs and error budgets, incident management
Programming and automation: Go, Python, Bash, GitHub Actions
Systems: Linux, Puppet, k6

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd (B2B accounting SaaS)
Manchester / remote | Apr 2022 – Present
- Tech lead for a five-person platform team, operating an AWS EKS platform across eight clusters and three regions, supporting approximately 350 services.
- Led development of an internal developer platform used by all 14 product teams, including Go and Python service templates, Argo CD GitOps, and Crossplane self-service provisioning for RDS, SQS and S3.
- Reduced the time to take a new service to production from approximately two weeks to under one day.
- Led migration from cluster-autoscaler managed node groups to Karpenter, using Spot instances for stateless workloads with interruption handling; reduced EC2 spend by 38% (approximately GBP 410,000 per year).
- Introduced SLOs, burn-rate alerts and error budgets for the 20 most critical services, agreeing the error-budget policy with product leadership. Reduced on-call pages by approximately 60%.
- Participate in the incident commander rotation and established the incident and post-mortem process.

Site Reliability Engineer | Brightwater Games
Leeds | Jan 2019 – Mar 2022
- Operated AWS game-backend infrastructure using EC2, ECS and later EKS for titles with up to 1.2 million daily active players.
- Managed AWS infrastructure as code using approximately 40 Terraform modules, with Atlantis for plan and apply workflows on pull requests.
- Replaced a noisy Nagios setup with a Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki observability stack.
- Used k6 load testing and launch-day capacity planning to prepare services for major launches. A test simulating 300,000 concurrent players identified a connection-pool limit that was fixed before launch.

Linux Systems Engineer | Pennine Hosting
Sheffield | Jul 2016 – Dec 2018
- Managed approximately 600 Linux servers for hosting customers using Puppet configuration management.
- Automated operational tasks with Bash and Python and provided on-call support for customer incidents.

SELECTED PROJECT
Kubernetes preview-namespace cleanup operator | Open source | 2024
- Built a small Go Kubernetes controller using controller-runtime to delete expired preview namespaces; the project has approximately 120 GitHub stars.

LEADERSHIP & SPEAKING
- Mentored three engineers transitioning from backend engineering into SRE.
- Speaker at a UK DevOps meetup in 2024: “SLOs that product managers care about”.

EDUCATION
BSc Computer Science | University of the North Moors | 2016

CERTIFICATIONS
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) | 2021; renewed 2024
AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional | 2023

LANGUAGES
English (native) | Urdu (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured technical CV with clear seniority, relevant scope, measurable outcomes, and credible platform/SRE experience. The strongest evidence includes operation of eight EKS clusters across three regions, support for approximately 350 services, an internal developer platform adopted by all 14 product teams, a 38% EC2 cost reduction, and a 60% reduction in on-call pages. The document is concise and professionally written, and the certification, speaking, mentoring, and open-source sections strengthen the leadership profile. The main content weakness is that several requirements central to this role—system design, networking security, and stakeholder-facing technical decision-making—are not explicitly evidenced. These appear primarily to be candidate-experience gaps rather than writing defects.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard headings, conventional reverse-chronological formatting, searchable text, and strong ATS keywords including AWS, EKS, Terraform, Kubernetes, GitOps, Crossplane, Prometheus, Linux, Go, Python, and incident management. The quantified achievements should parse well. ATS matching will be strong for AWS, infrastructure engineering, Kubernetes, Terraform, observability, reliability, and Linux, but weaker for the exact terms Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, system architecture, system design, and practical security. These terms should not be added unless supported by the candidate's actual experience. The headline and summary are effective, although the unsupported phrase about taking initiatives from “technical proposal through production” should be removed or reworded.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document is a strong match for hands-on cloud infrastructure, AWS environment operation, Terraform, Linux, reliability, observability, technical leadership, analytical problem-solving, and supporting developers with deployable services. It aligns well with Corvale's engineering-led, end-to-end ownership culture through evidence of platform ownership, self-service enablement, incident leadership, and collaboration with product leadership. The candidate's experience designing and operating Kubernetes/AWS platforms is relevant to the role's cloud infrastructure scope. However, the candidate information does not evidence Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, train/vehicle connectivity, IoT, automotive, remote-device integration, JVM development, or full-stack development. The CV also provides limited explicit evidence of broader systems architecture, network design, or security decision-making beyond AWS IAM and infrastructure operation. These are experience gaps, not defects that can be solved through wording.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL — In the Professional Summary section, remove or reword “leading platform initiatives from technical proposal through production,” because the Original Candidate Information does not explicitly substantiate ownership of technical proposals through production. For example, change it to “leading platform initiatives and operating them in production,” which is supported by the Tallybrook experience.

MINOR — In the Professional Summary or Core Skills section, use the exact supported phrase “cloud infrastructure design and operation” alongside the existing “designing, building and operating cloud infrastructure” wording. This will improve alignment with the job ad without adding an unsupported capability.

MINOR — In the Senior Platform Engineer entry under Tallybrook Ltd, retain the existing evidence about agreeing the error-budget policy with product leadership and consider changing “agreed the error-budget policy with product leadership” to “aligned the error-budget policy with product leadership.” This makes the stakeholder-influence aspect more direct while remaining truthful.
critique.critical_issues:
Potential unsupported claim: The Professional Summary states that the candidate has led platform initiatives “from technical proposal through production.” The Original Candidate Information supports technical leadership, platform ownership, production operation, and work with product leadership, but does not explicitly support ownership of technical proposals through production. Remove or reword this claim to avoid overstating experience.
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- "leading platform initiatives from technical proposal through production"
- "Led migration from cluster-autoscaler managed node groups to Karpenter"

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear progression from Linux systems engineering to senior platform leadership. It uses quantified outcomes effectively, including the reduction in service deployment time, 38% EC2 cost reduction, 60% reduction in on-call pages, scale across 350 services, and infrastructure supporting 1.2 million daily players. The main content limitation is that several useful details from the candidate information are omitted, particularly the 14-team adoption of the internal developer platform, the 300,000-concurrent-player load test, and the specific tools used in the SLO programme.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses standard section headings, conventional reverse-chronological experience formatting, readable text, and keyword-rich skills categories. AWS, EKS, Terraform, Kubernetes, Linux, observability, incident management, SLOs, and technical leadership are likely to match strongly in automated screening. AI screening probability is high for the platform/SRE aspects of this role. Matching will be weaker for exact terms that are absent from the candidate information or document, especially Terragrunt, mutual TLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, and security. These are genuine experience gaps rather than formatting defects. The use of slash-separated titles is acceptable, although the title could be kept consistent with the original wording for maximum clarity.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns very well with hands-on infrastructure engineering, AWS cloud environment operation, Terraform, Linux, observability, reliability, technical leadership, stakeholder alignment, and clear evidence-based problem solving. The internal developer platform and SLO work also fit Corvale's emphasis on end-to-end ownership, developer enablement, and leading technical topics from implementation through production. The document does not establish experience with Terragrunt, mTLS or SSL/TLS, certificate management, practical security work, IoT/automotive/remote-device integration, or JVM-based backend/full-stack development. Those are candidate-profile gaps and cannot be solved through wording alone. Networking is represented through AWS VPC and related services, and virtual-machine experience is reasonably supported by EC2, but the CV does not describe deeper networking or security responsibilities.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Senior Platform Engineer section under Tallybrook Ltd, revise the internal developer platform bullet to include its adoption scope: change it to mention that the platform was "used by all 14 product teams," while retaining the existing Go/Python templates, Argo CD GitOps, and Crossplane provisioning details. This strengthens evidence of stakeholder adoption and technical influence.
2. In the SLO bullet under Tallybrook Ltd, add the supported implementation details "Prometheus recording rules and Sloth" and, if space permits, "PagerDuty". For example: "Introduced SLOs, burn-rate alerts and error budgets for the 20 most critical services using Prometheus recording rules and Sloth; aligned the error-budget policy with product leadership and reduced on-call pages by approximately 60%." Do not add tools beyond those documented in the candidate information.
3. In the Site Reliability Engineer section under Brightwater Games, expand the k6 bullet to include the strongest analytical result from the candidate information: a test simulating "300,000 concurrent players" identified and enabled the team to fix a connection-pool limit before launch. This directly demonstrates analytical thinking, capacity planning, and production-readiness work.

This improves retrieval for the networking portion of the advert without claiming unsupported mTLS, SSL/TLS, or certificate-management experience.

In the Professional Summary, replace the slightly repetitive wording "including cloud infrastructure design and operation, and leading platform initiatives and operating them in production" with a tighter supported formulation such as: "with six years operating Kubernetes platforms on AWS and hands-on experience designing, building and operating cloud infrastructure and internal platforms in production."
